3) Deep validation and requirement scoping (REQ-SUPPORTS-VALIDATE, REQ-SCOPED-IDS, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT) - Implementation: src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts - IMPLEMENTS_TOKENS defines positions for story path and first requirement in @supports lines. - parseImplementsLine(line): * Splits line and returns { storyPath, reqIds } or null if missing path / IDs. - validateImplementsLine(...): * Uses resolveStoryAndRequirements(...) to validate/resolve storyPath and get a Set of requirements from that file (via loadAndCacheRequirements(...)). * Iterates over reqIds, calling checkRequirementExists(...) for each. * Thus, each requirement is validated against its specific story file, and IDs are scoped per file. - handleAnnotationLine(...) dispatches: * @story → update storyPath * @req → validateReqLine(...) using current storyPath * @supports → validateImplementsLine(...) - Error messages (include story path context): * reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'" * invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'" - Tests (tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts): - Valid @supports deep-validation: * Single @supports with multiple requirements in multi-story fixture, referencing 010.2. * Multiple @supports lines combining shared and story-specific REQ IDs, confirming per-story scoping. - Invalid @supports deep-validation: * Missing requirement in multi-story fixture → asserts messageId "reqMissing" with data { reqId, storyPath }. * Path traversal in supports story path → asserts messageId "invalidPath" with storyPath including the invalid value.
4) Rules accepting @supports as satisfying annotations and preserving backward compatibility (REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-SUPPORTS, REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT) - Story-annotation detection helpers: src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts - commentContainsStory(comment): returns true if value includes "@story" OR "@supports" (explicitly documented with story 010.2 and REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS). - scanLinesForMarker(...): treats lines containing "@story" or "@supports" as annotated. - fallbackTextBeforeHasStory(...): same behavior using raw text slice. - parentChainHasStory(...) uses commentContainsStory, so parent comments containing @supports count as story coverage. - require-story rule behavior: src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts and src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - hasStoryAnnotation(...) leverages the IO helpers above, so @supports alone prevents missingStory errors. - require-story-annotation.ts itself only enforces presence; detection is abstracted, so no code change needed to accept @supports. - Requirement-annotation detection helpers: src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts - commentContainsReq(...) accepts both "@req" and "@supports". - linesBeforeHasReq(...), parentChainHasReq(...), fallbackTextBeforeHasReq(...) all look for "@req" OR "@supports". - hasReqAnnotation(...) returns true if any heuristic finds @req or @supports, or if jsdoc includes either. - require-req rule behavior: src/utils/annotation-checker.ts and src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts - checkReqAnnotation(...) uses hasReqAnnotation(...); therefore @supports satisfies requirement presence. - Tests: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts * Header cites story 010.2 and REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS. * Valid case: "[REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS] valid with only @implements annotation" with code that has only @supports — no missingStory error. * Invalid case for backward compatibility: - "[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED][BACKCOMPAT] missing @story annotation on function with no @supports" — confirms unannotated functions remain invalid. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts * Header cites story 010.2 and REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS. * Valid case: "[REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS] valid with only @implements annotation" with only @supports. * Invalid case: missing @req with no annotations remains an error, confirming backward compatibility.
5) Mixed usage of annotation styles in same file/comment (REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT) - Implementation: - valid-annotation-format.ts: * processCommentLine(...) handles @supports immediately, while still accumulating @story/@req multi-line values, enabling mixed blocks. * JSDoc on processComment and processCommentLine lists REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT and mentions supporting mixed @story/@req/@supports. - valid-req-reference.ts: * handleAnnotationLine(...) and processCommentLines(...) handle comments with intermixed @story, @req, and @supports lines. - Tests: - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts * Explicit mixed-usage test: "[REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT] valid mixed @story/@req/@supports usage in same block comment".
6) Error messages for requirement validation include story context (REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT) - Format-level @supports errors (valid-annotation-format.ts): - reportInvalidImplementsStoryPath(...) message details include the problematic storyPath and example path. - Deep validation errors (valid-req-reference.ts): - reqMissing and invalidPath messages both interpolate storyPath, and tests assert on data.storyPath for @supports scenarios.
7) Documentation and migration guidance (Documentation AC) - user-docs/migration-guide.md: - Section "3.1 Multi-story `@supports` annotations" explains: * The @supports format and a concrete example. * That @story + @req remain valid. * When to use @supports (multi-story integration) vs. keep legacy style. * How to gradually introduce @supports and mix both styles during migration, including an example function containing both. - README.md: - Mentions optional rule "traceability/prefer-implements-annotation" now used to migrate legacy @story/@req to @supports. - ADR 011-rename-implements-to-supports-annotation.accepted.md: - Confirms @supports is the canonical user-facing multi-story annotation. - States that @implements is no longer recognized in user code and that semantics (scoped IDs, multi-story behavior, backward compatibility) remain unchanged.
8) Quality standards (rule structure, testing, backward compatibility) - ESLint rules follow best practices: proper meta, schemas, clear separation of helpers, and strong Jest coverage tied to this story. - No remaining usage of @implements as a user annotation; all user-visible behavior centers on @supports, consistent with ADR 011 and the story. - All relevant tests for single-story, multi-story, and mixed usage scenarios are present and passing, satisfying the Definition of Done items that are within this repo (tests and backward compatibility via the suite).
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and requirements in docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md are implemented and verified. The plugin parses and validates @supports annotations (format and syntax), deep-validates each listed requirement against the correct story file with requirement IDs scoped per story, and updates the require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation rules so that @supports satisfies story and requirement presence checks while preserving existing @story/@req behavior. Mixed usage of both annotation styles in the same file/comment is supported and tested. Error messages for both format and deep-validation failures include the relevant story path, and user-facing documentation (migration guide and ADR 011) clearly explains @supports usage and migration from legacy annotations. All linked tests for this story pass, so the story is fully implemented.
